A friend borrowed $5,000 from me for his catering truck and signed a one-page note promising to repay by his birthday. The last payment he made was just under three years ago. In my state the deadline to sue on a signed loan note is three years from the last payment, and that falls 18 days from today. I should say that this has not been a gloomy stretch for him otherwise. He got married in June, and his truck won a local best-street-food award in August, which got him a feature in the weekend paper and a flood of bookings for fall weddings. I went to his reception and ate more brisket than I'd like to admit. We also play in the same Thursday-night pickup soccer league, and his team has been on a winning streak that has everybody teasing him about it. His mother still sends me jars of pickled peppers every few months, and my kids adore his younger sister, who babysits for us. Honestly the whole circle of friends overlaps so much that I'd rather not turn up the heat on anything before the busy season settles. Last week I helped him carry a folding table into his storage unit, and he told me about a plan to add a second truck next spring if the bookings hold. He seemed relaxed and happy, and the whole afternoon felt like old times. I left with a bag of leftover rolls and a promise to come by for the next tasting event.

I'm going to give him space until his catering season ends in the fall. What's the plan?

A) File a small claims case this week to protect my right to collect
B) Ask a lawyer or the court's self-help center how the deadline works before deciding
C) Wait until the fall and let him pay voluntarily

I'm furious and want a couple of weeks to cool down before I decide anything about the case. What's the plan?

A) Set a reminder and come back to it in two weeks
B) File the notice of appeal today and decide later whether to pursue it
